commands.name: /add-dir
commands.summary: Give this session file access to another folder.
commands.details: Adds a working directory so Claude can read and edit files there for the rest of the session. Most .claude configuration inside that folder is not picked up. Without a terminal it is only offered to cloud, SSH and other remote-hosted sessions.

signalbox.note: Changes what a live session can reach; run it in that session.

commands.name: /advisor
commands.summary: Let Claude consult a second, stronger model at key points of a task.
commands.details: Name the advisor (fable, opus, sonnet or a full model id), or pass off to stop using one. Bare, the terminal opens a picker and other surfaces print the current choice. Experimental: it appears only when the advisor is turned on for your account, and only on the Anthropic API.
commands.sideEffects: In a terminal session it saves the advisor as your default for every session (advisorModel in ~/.claude/settings.json). Only from Remote Control does it change just this session. Advisor calls add to usage.

signalbox.note: `/advisor <model>` or `/advisor off` through the opt-in session mod, labelled as changing your default advisor.

commands.name: /agents
commands.summary: Removed: now only says to ask Claude, or edit the agents folders, to manage subagents.
commands.details: Up to 2.1.197 this opened a subagent manager. In 2.1.293 it is hidden and only prints a reminder about .claude/agents/ and ~/.claude/agents/.

signalbox.note: Signalbox doesn't manage subagent files. For background sessions see Sessions or `claude agents`.

commands.name: /artifact-capabilities
commands.summary: Skill: reference for what a published artifact page can do at runtime.
commands.details: Bundled skill Claude normally loads by itself before building an artifact that needs live data, storage or downloads. Only where artifacts are available.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /artifact-components
commands.summary: Skill: embed reusable components in an artifact.
commands.details: Bundled skill present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page. Only enabled where artifacts and its feature flag are on.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /artifact-diagramming
commands.summary: Skill: diagram guidance for artifacts, with inline SVG that reads in both themes.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /artifacts
commands.summary: Browse artifacts you own or that are shared with you; attach, open or copy a link.
commands.details: Only where artifacts are available. Enter attaches the chosen artifact to the session.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /auto-mode-setup
commands.summary: Draft auto-mode environment notes from your project, review, save to settings.
commands.details: Looks at the project and recent sessions to describe your environment for the auto-mode classifier, then lets you review the draft. Needs a Pro, Max or Team plan. Headless and Remote Control get a flag-driven form instead of the dialog.
commands.sideEffects: Writes autoMode entries to your user settings.

signalbox.note: Changes what auto mode lets Claude do without asking; Signalbox won't send it.

commands.name: /autocompact
commands.summary: Set how full the context window gets before Claude Code compacts on its own.
commands.details: Give a size such as 500k, or auto to go back to the default window for your model. Bare, the terminal opens a dialog and other surfaces print the current window.
commands.sideEffects: Saved in your user settings for the current model only, so later sessions on that model use it too. Other models keep their own window.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows where auto-compact kicks in when known. A slider marked as applying to this model in every session, sent as `/autocompact <N>` through the opt-in session mod, is planned.

commands.name: /autofix-pr
commands.summary: Start a cloud session that watches this branch's PR and pushes fixes.
commands.details: Finds the PR for the checked-out branch with gh and, by default, works on every failing check and review comment; a prompt narrows that. You need the gh CLI installed and cloud sessions turned on for your account.
commands.sideEffects: Creates a cloud session that pushes commits to your PR branch.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /background
commands.summary: Hand this session off to run in the background and get your terminal back.
commands.details: Optionally sends one more instruction first. Follow it later with `claude agents`, `claude attach` or `claude logs`. Use /fork to copy the session instead of moving it.

signalbox.note: Background sessions show up in Sessions; detaching happens in the terminal.

commands.name: /batch
commands.summary: Skill: plan a large change, then run parallel worktree agents that each ship a part.
commands.details: It studies the codebase, breaks the job into 5 to 30 pieces that don't depend on each other, and asks you to approve the plan. After you approve, each unit gets a background subagent in its own worktree that implements, tests and publishes its change. Needs a git repository or a WorktreeCreate hook.
commands.sideEffects: Creates worktrees and background agents; each one publishes its change, usually as a PR.

signalbox.note: Long multi-agent job; start it in the session. Its agents appear in Sessions.

commands.name: /branch
commands.summary: Branch the conversation here and switch to the copy; the original stays resumable.
commands.details: Use it to try another direction without losing the conversation as it stands. /fork copies into a separate background session instead; /subtask hands a side task to a subagent.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /brief
commands.summary: Toggle brief-only mode, where Claude talks to you through a message tool.
commands.details: Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not in the docs. Only enabled when a server-side setting allows it; otherwise it says the tool is not enabled for your account.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /btw
commands.summary: Ask a quick question on the side; the answer stays out of the main conversation.
commands.details: With no question it shows your recent side questions. In the desktop app it opens a side chat.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /bug
commands.summary: Report a bug, optionally with session history, after a consent screen.
commands.details: You choose how much history to include. Signed in to Anthropic, the report goes to Anthropic; otherwise it is saved under ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ for you to forward.
commands.sideEffects: Can send parts of your conversation to Anthropic.

signalbox.note: Shares conversation data; only you should send it, from the session.

commands.name: /cd
commands.summary: Switch this session to a different folder without losing the conversation.
commands.details: Unlike /add-dir, the session's working directory changes and settings from the new folder apply.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /chrome
commands.summary: Open settings for Claude in Chrome, the browser extension Claude can drive.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /claim-credit
commands.summary: Open the offer page advertised when Claude Code started.
commands.details: Hidden; only when an offer is active. Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not in the docs.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /claude-api
commands.summary: Skill: brings in Claude API and Managed Agents docs that match your code's language.
commands.details: Also loads by itself when code imports the Anthropic SDK. It can't be typed from a Remote Control client, though Claude can still load it there.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /claude-code-docs
commands.summary: Skill: answer questions about Claude Code features and settings.
commands.details: Bundled skill present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page. It reads the official docs and is told which build is running.

signalbox.note: Ask it in a session.

commands.name: /claude-in-chrome
commands.summary: Skill: have Claude do a task in your Chrome browser.
commands.details: Clicks, fills forms, takes screenshots and reads console logs through the Claude in Chrome extension. Available when Chrome integration is on for the session, for example with --chrome.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /clear
commands.summary: Start a new conversation with empty context; the old one stays resumable.
commands.details: Give it a name and the old conversation shows under that name when you /resume. Project memory is kept. To keep going in the same conversation with less context, use /compact.
commands.sideEffects: The session continues under a new conversation id and its cost counter starts again.

signalbox.note: Drops the working context; run it yourself in the session. Signalbox keeps counting spend across the change.

commands.name: /cloud-plugins
commands.summary: Decide whether plugins turned on here also load in your cloud sessions.
commands.details: Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page; only enabled when plugin forwarding to cloud sessions is on.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /code-review
commands.summary: Skill: review the diff, a PR, branch or path for bugs; can apply or post findings.
commands.details: The level sets how deep it goes; with none it reuses the last level you typed. --fix applies the findings, --comment posts them to the GitHub PR or GitLab MR, and ultra runs a cloud review (the same as /ultrareview).
commands.sideEffects: --fix edits files, --comment posts to your PR, and ultra uses cloud review runs or usage credits.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /color
commands.summary: Set this session's prompt bar color; no argument picks a random one.
commands.details: default resets it. Over Remote Control, claude.ai/code shows the same color.
commands.sideEffects: Applies to this session only.

signalbox.note: A color chip on the session card, sent as `/color <c>` through the opt-in session mod.

commands.name: /commit
commands.summary: Skill: make a git commit with the repo's context and commit rules.
commands.details: Bundled skill in the 2.1.293 binary that is rolled out gradually and isn't on the commands page. Claude can also use it when a task reaches a commit.
commands.sideEffects: Creates a git commit.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /compact
commands.summary: Summarize the conversation so far to free context; optional focus instructions.
commands.details: Runs a model call that replaces earlier messages with a summary; key rules, skills and memory files are carried over. Auto-compaction does the same when the window fills.
commands.sideEffects: Uses a model call; earlier messages are no longer in context afterwards.

signalbox.note: Sessions already lists each compaction (manual or auto, tokens before). A 'compact now' button with a focus field is planned through the opt-in session mod.

commands.name: /config
commands.summary: Open settings, or set keys directly with key=value.
commands.details: The key=value form also works in -p and from the mobile app over Remote Control; `/config --help` lists the keys. It can't switch on settings that need a confirmation in the panel. In the desktop app it opens Settings and ignores arguments.
commands.sideEffects: key=value writes your user settings, which affects every session.

signalbox.note: Writes global Claude Code settings; Signalbox never changes agent config.

commands.name: /context
commands.summary: Show what's filling the context window, with tips to free space.
commands.details: The terminal draws a colored grid; other surfaces print text. It warns when the conversation is already over the window. all expands the per-item breakdown in fullscreen.

signalbox.note: Each session row has a context gauge (tokens, window, percent, auto-compact point) from what the agent records, without running /context.

commands.name: /copy
commands.summary: Copy Claude's last (or Nth-latest) reply to the clipboard, or pick code blocks.
commands.details: When the reply has code blocks a picker lets you choose; w writes the selection to a file instead.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /daemon
commands.summary: Control the background worker service and the routines it runs.
commands.details: Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not in the docs; only turned on when the background worker registry is enabled for you.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /dataviz
commands.summary: Skill: chart and dashboard design guidance with a checked, colorblind-safe palette.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /debug
commands.summary: Skill: turn on debug logging for this session and diagnose a problem from the log.
commands.details: Logging starts when you run it, unless the session was started with --debug. Add a description of the problem to narrow what it looks at.
commands.sideEffects: Writes a debug log for the session.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /deep-research
commands.summary: Workflow: fan out web searches, cross-check sources, write a cited report.
commands.details: A bundled dynamic workflow that runs many subagents in the background; watch it with /workflows. Needs dynamic workflows to be enabled. Claude never starts it on its own; you have to type it.
commands.sideEffects: Runs many subagents and web fetches, so it uses a lot of tokens.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /design
commands.summary: Skill: draft UI mockups or posters as artboards in a Claude Design artifact.
commands.details: Needs artifacts and the Design template on your account; not available on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /design-consent
commands.summary: Allow Claude agents to open and work with your Claude Design projects.
commands.details: Hidden from the menu. Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page.

signalbox.note: Account authorization; only you should grant it.

commands.name: /design-login
commands.summary: Authorize /design-sync to use your claude.ai account for design systems.

signalbox.note: Account authorization; only you should grant it.

commands.name: /design-revoke
commands.summary: Stop Claude agents from reaching your Claude Design projects.
commands.details: Hidden from the menu. Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page.

signalbox.note: Account authorization; only you should change it.

commands.name: /design-sync
commands.summary: Skill: convert your repo's React design system and upload it to Claude Design.
commands.details: The first sync goes through every component, which can take hours in a big repo. Needs claude.ai, so it is unavailable on third-party providers.
commands.sideEffects: Uploads your component code to claude.ai/design.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /desktop
commands.summary: Hand this session to the Claude desktop app and close the CLI.
commands.details: macOS and x64 Windows with a Claude subscription. From a shell, `claude --desktop` opens the app without starting a terminal session.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /diff
commands.summary: Review uncommitted changes and per-turn diffs, including Claude's edits.

signalbox.note: Shows file contents; Signalbox doesn't read code or messages.

commands.name: /doctor
commands.summary: Skill: check your setup (install, settings, extensions, CLAUDE.md) and fix issues.
commands.details: Proposes fixes and applies them after you confirm. prompt-audit reviews your instruction files instead.
commands.sideEffects: Can change settings, extensions and memory files after you confirm.

signalbox.note: Signalbox's Health view covers its own data sources, not Claude Code's install. Run /doctor in a session, or `claude doctor` for a read-only check.

commands.name: /effort
commands.summary: Set reasoning effort (low to xhigh, max, auto); status prints the level.
commands.details: max lasts for this session only. ultracode switches ultracode on for the session at the current level. Changing effort mid-session can mean rebuilding the prompt cache.
commands.sideEffects: In an interactive session a level such as /effort high becomes your default for this model in new sessions, and /effort auto clears it. max and ultracode on/off last for this session only. In -p nothing is saved.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows each session's effort. A segmented control sending `/effort <level>` through the opt-in session mod is planned, with a warning that it changes your default effort for this model, as /model does.

commands.name: /exit
commands.summary: Quit Claude Code; in an attached background session it detaches instead.

signalbox.note: Ends a session; Signalbox won't do that for you.

commands.name: /explain-usage
commands.summary: Skill: explain where this session's tokens went, in plain words.
commands.details: Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page; only enabled on some hosted surfaces.

signalbox.note: Usage breaks spend down by model, project, day and kind from local transcripts.

commands.name: /export
commands.summary: Save the conversation as plain text to a file or the clipboard.
commands.sideEffects: Writes the whole conversation to a file or the clipboard.

signalbox.note: Holds message content, which Signalbox never reads or shows.

commands.name: /fast
commands.summary: Turn fast mode on or off: faster Opus replies at a higher price.
commands.details: Takes effect without waiting for the turn to end, though the running turn keeps its speed. Only Opus 5.5, Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 support it. Support in -p is limited.
commands.sideEffects: In the terminal the choice carries over to new sessions. On Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise, fast mode is paid from usage credits, not your plan, and costs more per token.

signalbox.note: Signalbox leaves this to you because it changes what you pay; on subscription plans it draws on usage credits. Run it in the session.

commands.name: /feedback
commands.summary: Send product feedback through the same consent dialog as /bug.
commands.details: When Claude has drafted feedback for you, running it with no argument opens that drafts queue.
commands.sideEffects: Can send parts of your conversation to Anthropic.

signalbox.note: Shares conversation data; only you should send it, from the session.

commands.name: /fewer-permission-prompts
commands.summary: Skill: find safe read-only commands in your transcripts and allowlist them.
commands.sideEffects: Writes allow rules to the project's .claude/settings.json.

signalbox.note: Changes permission rules.

commands.name: /focus
commands.summary: Toggle focus view: just your prompt, a tool summary and the final reply.
commands.details: Fullscreen renderer only, and the choice persists across sessions. From a Remote Control client, on or off applies to the current session only.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /fork
commands.summary: Make a copy of this chat that keeps running in the background while you carry on here.
commands.details: With a prompt the copy starts on it right away; it is told to use its own worktree before editing. When agent view is off, /fork starts a forked subagent instead.
commands.sideEffects: Starts a new background session.

signalbox.note: The copy appears in Sessions as a background session.

commands.name: /goal
commands.summary: Set a goal: Claude keeps working across turns until the condition is met.
commands.details: With no argument it shows the current or last goal; clear, stop, off or cancel removes it.
commands.sideEffects: Claude keeps taking turns until the goal is met, which adds usage.

signalbox.note: Starts open-ended work; set it in the session. A session waiting on a goal proposal shows as waiting in Sessions.

commands.name: /heapdump
commands.summary: Write a memory heap snapshot and breakdown to your Desktop.
commands.details: Not listed in the menu, so type the full name. When reporting a memory problem, share only the -diagnostics.json file, never the .heapsnapshot.
commands.sideEffects: Writes a large file that can contain credentials and the full conversation.

signalbox.note: The snapshot can hold credentials and the whole conversation.

commands.name: /help
commands.summary: List the commands you can use, each with a short explanation.

signalbox.note: This guide plays that role in Signalbox, for every surface.

commands.name: /hooks
commands.summary: Browse the hooks you have set up, grouped by the tool event they run on.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /ide
commands.summary: See and manage the connection to your code editor.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /import
commands.summary: Bring config from Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor into Claude Code.
commands.details: Covers instruction files, MCP servers, commands, subagents and skills. --dry-run previews; in -p it lists what it found and prints the command that confirms. Needs feature flags and isn't offered on third-party providers.
commands.sideEffects: Writes Claude Code config files unless --dry-run.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /init
commands.summary: Generate a starter CLAUDE.md for the project from the codebase.
commands.details: With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 it also walks through skills, hooks and personal memory. It offers /import when it finds Codex or Gemini CLI config.
commands.sideEffects: Writes CLAUDE.md.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /insights
commands.summary: Generate an HTML report on your recent sessions: projects, habits, problem spots.
commands.details: Analyzes the sessions on this machine with a model, so it costs usage. Cloud sessions don't have it.
commands.sideEffects: Uses a model call and writes a report under ~/.claude/usage-data/.

signalbox.note: Usage covers spend without a model call; run /insights yourself for the behaviour report.

commands.name: /install-github-app
commands.summary: Set up the Claude GitHub App and an optional Actions workflow for a repo.
commands.details: github.com repositories only; on GitLab or Bitbucket it prints a notice and stops.
commands.sideEffects: Installs a GitHub App and can add workflow files and secrets.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /install-slack-app
commands.summary: Install the Claude Slack app through a browser sign-in flow.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /keybindings
commands.summary: Edit your custom keyboard shortcuts in their config file.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /limit-reset
commands.summary: Use an available limit reset to refill your session limit and keep working.
commands.details: Hidden; offered only on some claude.ai plans, about once a week, and it still counts toward the weekly limit. Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not in the docs.

signalbox.note: Spends a scarce reset; only you should decide that.

commands.name: /list-agents
commands.summary: Show who this session can message: subagents, teammates and other sessions.
commands.details: Only where cross-session messaging is enabled. Shows the name to use when messaging each one.

signalbox.note: Sessions lists live and background sessions on this machine from `claude agents --json` and the session registry.

commands.name: /login
commands.summary: Sign in to your Anthropic account, or switch accounts.

signalbox.note: Handles credentials.

commands.name: /logout
commands.summary: End your Anthropic sign-in on this machine.

signalbox.note: Handles credentials.

commands.name: /loop
commands.summary: Skill: repeat a prompt or command on an interval while the session stays open.
commands.details: Leave out the interval and Claude picks its own pace; leave out the prompt and it runs a maintenance prompt or your loop.md. For instance: `/loop 10m run the tests and report failures`.
commands.sideEffects: Each run is a model turn, so usage keeps adding up.

signalbox.note: Recurring work; start it in the session. Limits shows how fast it uses the 5-hour window.

commands.name: /low-priority
commands.summary: After hitting a session limit, keep going at lower priority; run again to stop.
commands.details: Hidden; offered only on some claude.ai plans. Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not in the docs.

signalbox.note: Limits shows the window; this choice stays in the session.

commands.name: /mcp
commands.summary: Manage MCP servers: list, sign in, reconnect, enable or disable.
commands.details: No argument opens the interactive list in a terminal and prints a status summary elsewhere. reconnect all tries again every server that failed or is waiting for sign-in.

signalbox.note: Only `/mcp reconnect <server>` is a candidate for the opt-in session mod; Signalbox doesn't show MCP status yet.

commands.name: /memory
commands.summary: Edit CLAUDE.md files, toggle auto memory and view saved memories.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /mobile
commands.summary: Show a QR code that leads to the Claude app for your phone.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /model
commands.summary: Switch model; in the terminal it also becomes your default for new sessions.
commands.details: Bare, it opens a picker, where s on a row changes only this session. In -p and SDK hosts such as the desktop app, pass the model as an argument and only the current session changes. Switching can mean rebuilding the prompt cache.
commands.sideEffects: In an interactive session (also when sent over Remote Control) it saves your default model; in -p and SDK hosts it is session-only.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows each session's model. A per-session picker is planned, with a warning that it can change your global default.

commands.name: /output-style
commands.summary: Show the available output styles, or change the one this project uses.
commands.details: From Remote Control only the built-in styles can be listed and picked.
commands.sideEffects: Saves the style in this project's .claude/settings.local.json, so later sessions in the project start with it too.

signalbox.note: The argument form, `/output-style <style>`, is a candidate for the opt-in session mod, labelled as changing this project's local settings.

commands.name: /passes
commands.summary: Share a free week of Claude Code with friends (eligible accounts only).

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /permissions
commands.summary: Manage allow, ask and deny rules for tools, plus auto-mode rules and denials.

signalbox.note: Changes what Claude may do without asking.

commands.name: /plan
commands.summary: Enter plan mode; with a description, start planning that task right away.
commands.details: open shows the current plan. In plan mode Claude reads and plans without editing until you approve.

signalbox.note: Permission mode is chosen in the session; the desktop app has its own mode selector.

commands.name: /plugin
commands.summary: Manage plugins and marketplaces: list, install, enable, disable.
commands.details: In the desktop app it points you to the app's own plugin manager instead. From a shell, `claude plugin ...` does the same jobs.

signalbox.note: Signalbox lists commands and skills from your enabled plugins in this guide; managing them stays in the session or `claude plugin`.

commands.name: /plugin-authoring
commands.summary: Skill: the reference Claude uses to write a mod (hooks, panes, status lines).
commands.details: Comes from a built-in plugin that you can turn off in /plugin.

signalbox.note: Reference material for Claude; nothing for Signalbox to run.

commands.name: /powerup
commands.summary: Short interactive lessons with animated demos of Claude Code features.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /privacy-settings
commands.summary: View and change your privacy settings (Pro and Max).

signalbox.note: Account data-sharing choices; only you should change them.

commands.name: /prototype
commands.summary: Skill: prototype an idea as a working artifact.
commands.details: Present in the 2.1.293 binary but not on the commands page; gated to accounts with artifacts and this feature.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /radio
commands.summary: Play Claude FM, a lo-fi music stream, in your web browser.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /rate-limit-options
commands.summary: When a claude.ai limit blocks you: wait and continue, add credits, or upgrade.
commands.details: Claude Code can also open it by itself when you hit a limit. Only for people signed in with a claude.ai plan.

signalbox.note: Limits shows how close each window is and when it resets; this menu stays in the session.

commands.name: /recap
commands.summary: Write a one-line summary of the session now.
commands.details: It runs only when you type it yourself, in the session or over Remote Control; requests relayed from Slack, Teams, routines or other programs are turned away.
commands.sideEffects: May use a small model call.

commands.name: /release-notes
commands.summary: Browse the changelog by version.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.

commands.name: /reload-skills
commands.summary: Rescan skill and command folders so new or edited skills show up.

commands.details: Only for people signed in with a claude.ai plan. Running it again shows the link, a QR code and a way to disconnect.
commands.sideEffects: Makes the session available to your claude.ai account on other devices.

commands.name: /remote-env
commands.summary: Set which cloud environment new cloud sessions from the CLI use by default.

signalbox.note: Interactive; copy it and run it in the session.
