commands.name: /model
commands.summary: Pick the model and reasoning effort for this chat.
commands.details: Opens a picker with the models your account can use, plus a reasoning-effort choice where the model supports one. Codex can also store the pick as your default model in config.toml and tells you when a higher-priority config layer overrides it. Works while a task is running.
commands.sideEffects: Can save the chosen model as your default in ~/.codex/config.toml.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows each Codex session's current model. Switching it happens inside the session, and it may rewrite your default model.

commands.name: /fast
commands.summary: Turn the model's Fast service tier on or off, when the catalog offers one.
commands.details: Not a fixed command: Codex builds it from the model catalog and lists it right after /model only when the current model advertises a Fast tier. Other tier names can appear the same way. Running it again turns the tier off, and the choice is saved as the default service tier.
commands.sideEffects: Saves the default service tier in config.toml. Fast requests use more of your limits.

signalbox.note: Only available inside a session.

commands.name: /daybreak
commands.summary: Turn Daybreak, OpenAI's trusted cyber-access program, on or off for new turns.
commands.details: Hidden unless the cli_daybreak feature flag is on, which it is not by default in 0.161.0. It needs a ChatGPT sign-in, the OpenAI provider and an account approved for the program. The choice is saved for the thread and as a default preference.
commands.sideEffects: Saves a per-thread and a default Daybreak preference.

signalbox.note: Security-sensitive account program; Signalbox stays out of it.

commands.name: /ide
commands.summary: Add your IDE's open files and current selection to what Codex sees.
commands.details: Connects to the Codex IDE extension. Once on, the active file, the selection and open tabs ride along with later messages. /ide status reports the connection and /ide off stops it. Also works inside a side chat.

signalbox.note: Depends on the session's own IDE connection.

commands.name: /permissions
commands.summary: Choose what Codex may do without asking, such as Read Only or Auto.
commands.details: Opens a picker of approval and sandbox presets, plus any named permission profiles from your config with their descriptions. The new policy applies to the session's later actions until you change it again.
commands.sideEffects: Changes what the agent can run or write without asking.

signalbox.note: What an agent may do is the session owner's call, made in the session.

commands.name: /keymap
commands.summary: Inspect and remap the TUI's keyboard shortcuts.
commands.details: Opens a picker by context and action; a new binding is written to tui.keymap in config.toml, and an empty binding unbinds the action. /keymap debug shows how the current keymap resolves.
commands.sideEffects: Writes custom bindings to tui.keymap in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /vim
commands.summary: Toggle Vim editing in the prompt box for this session.
commands.details: Switches the composer between Vim normal/insert behaviour and the default editor. To start every session in Vim mode, set tui.vim_mode_default in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /setup-default-sandbox
commands.summary: Windows only: install the stronger, elevated sandbox for the agent.
commands.details: Only appears on native Windows while Codex is using its weaker fallback sandbox. It runs an administrator setup and then selects the Auto approval preset. It never shows on macOS.
commands.sideEffects: Administrator-level change to the Windows sandbox setup.

signalbox.note: System-level security change.

commands.name: /experimental
commands.summary: Turn experimental features on or off.
commands.details: Lists experimental toggles such as the network proxy or keeping the computer awake while a task runs. Choices are saved to config.toml, and some only apply after a restart.
commands.sideEffects: Saves feature flags to config.toml.

signalbox.note: Changes agent config; do it in the session or with codex features.

commands.name: /approve
commands.summary: Allow one retry of an action the automatic reviewer recently denied.
commands.details: Lists recent auto-review denials in this thread. Picking one records approval for a single retry; the model sees that approval and the retry still goes through auto-review. Only useful when automatic review is on.
commands.sideEffects: Lets a denied command or action run once more.

signalbox.note: Approvals are answered by the person in the session, never from outside.

commands.name: /memories
commands.summary: Choose whether Codex uses memories and whether it creates new ones.
commands.details: Has separate switches for using existing memories and for generating memories from this and later threads, plus a reset that clears local memory files and summaries. Settings are saved to config.toml and mostly take effect from the next thread.
commands.sideEffects: Saves memory settings to config.toml; the reset deletes local memory files.

signalbox.note: Agent setting; change it in the session.

commands.name: /skills
commands.summary: Browse skills, switch them on or off, or pick one to use.
commands.details: Opens the skills menu with the skills Codex found in user, repo, admin, bundled and plugin locations. You can also call a skill by typing $ and its name in the prompt. Switching a skill off is saved in config.toml.
commands.sideEffects: Toggling a skill updates skills settings in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Signalbox lists your own and plugin skills by name and description, but cannot run them.

commands.name: /import
commands.summary: Bring setup, project files and recent chats over from Claude Code.
commands.details: Opens a picker of what Codex can migrate: settings and instructions, MCP servers, agents, slash commands and skills, project files, and chats from the last 30 days. Codex adds its own files and leaves the original setup alone. Unavailable while a task runs and in remote or background-server sessions.
commands.sideEffects: Writes Codex config and may add files to the current project.

signalbox.note: Interactive picker in the session.

commands.name: /hooks
commands.summary: View lifecycle hooks and trust, disable or re-enable them.
commands.details: Opens a hook browser grouped by event, such as before a tool runs or when a session starts. New or changed hooks must be trusted before they run. Managed hooks are listed but cannot be switched off here.
commands.sideEffects: Saves hook trust and enabled state.

signalbox.note: Trusting code to run is a decision made in the session.

commands.name: /review
commands.summary: Ask Codex to review your changes and report problems.
commands.details: Without text it asks what to review: uncommitted changes, a base branch, a commit, or custom instructions. With text it starts a review that follows that text. It runs a model turn, using review_model from config when set. From a shell, codex review does the same.

signalbox.note: Starts a model turn. Run it in the session, or codex review in a terminal.

commands.name: /rename
commands.summary: Give the current chat a new name.
commands.details: With a name it renames at once; without one it opens a prompt. The transcript is unchanged. The name shows in session pickers and works with codex resume <name>.

signalbox.note: Changes the session; do it there.

commands.name: /new
commands.summary: Start a fresh chat in the same Codex window.
commands.details: The current chat stays saved. When worktrees are available, Codex asks whether the new chat runs in the current directory or in a new managed worktree. A name after the command titles the new chat. Unlike /clear, the screen is not wiped.

signalbox.note: Happens inside the session.

commands.name: /archive
commands.summary: Archive the session you're in, then quit Codex.
commands.details: Asks for confirmation, then removes the session from active lists and closes the TUI. The transcript stays on disk, and codex unarchive <SESSION> brings it back. Not available while a task runs or inside a side chat.
commands.sideEffects: Moves the session out of active session lists.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not change sessions it did not create.

commands.name: /delete
commands.summary: Permanently delete this session and its subagent sessions, then exit.
commands.details: Asks for confirmation first. The transcript and every subagent thread it spawned are removed and cannot be recovered. Not available while a task runs or inside a side chat.
commands.sideEffects: Deletes the session's files for good.

signalbox.note: Destructive.

commands.name: /resume
commands.summary: Reopen a saved chat from the session picker.
commands.details: Without arguments it opens the saved-session picker; with a session id or name it opens that session directly. The saved history is kept as it was. In a shell, codex resume does the same.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never resumes sessions. Select the session in History and use Copy under Resume, then paste the line (`cd` to its folder, then `codex resume <id>`) into a terminal.

commands.name: /fork
commands.summary: Copy the current chat into a new chat with its own id.
commands.details: The original transcript is left alone, so you can try another approach in parallel. When worktrees are available, Codex asks where the fork should run. To fork a different saved session, run codex fork in a shell.

signalbox.note: Happens inside the session.

commands.name: /worktree
commands.summary: Start or continue a chat in a separate Git worktree that Codex manages.
commands.details: Opens a picker of this repository's Codex-managed worktrees: create one, resume the chat that owns one, copy its path, or delete it. Deleting a worktree keeps the thread history. Needs a Git repository and the worktrees feature, which is on by default.
commands.sideEffects: Creates or deletes Git worktrees.

signalbox.note: Interactive picker in the session.

commands.name: /app
commands.summary: Continue this session in the ChatGPT desktop app (macOS and Windows).
commands.details: Opens the same saved chat in the desktop app. If the app is not installed or not running, Codex shows an error; codex app in a shell installs or opens it.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /init
commands.summary: Have Codex write an AGENTS.md with instructions for this project.
commands.details: Sends a built-in prompt asking the model to study the project and create AGENTS.md in the current directory. It costs a model turn, and the file is worth reviewing before you commit it.
commands.sideEffects: Creates AGENTS.md in the current directory.

signalbox.note: Starts a model turn in the session.

commands.name: /compact
commands.summary: Summarize the chat so far to free up context.
commands.details: Codex asks the model to condense the earlier turns and carries on from that summary, which keeps a long session under the context limit. It uses a model call and is not available while a task is running.

signalbox.note: Signalbox shows each session's context use and when it compacted, but Codex has no opt-in way for it to trigger compaction.

commands.name: /recap
commands.summary: Get a short, model-written summary of where this chat stands.
commands.details: Writes a recap of a few dozen words, including the next action, which helps when you come back to a session. It costs a model call and is not available while a task is running.

signalbox.note: Costs a model call; run it in the session.

commands.name: /plan
commands.summary: Switch to Plan mode, optionally with a first planning request.
commands.details: In Plan mode Codex proposes a plan before changing anything. Text after the command, along with pasted content or images, is sent as the first planning request. Not available while Codex is working.

signalbox.note: Changes how the session works; do it there.

commands.name: /voice
commands.summary: Start or stop a voice conversation; /voice settings picks a voice.
commands.details: Toggles a realtime voice session with Codex. /voice settings chooses the voice and sound devices, /voice mute mutes the microphone and /voice stop ends the conversation. Shown only when voice is available.

signalbox.note: Needs the session's microphone and speakers.

commands.name: /goal
commands.summary: Set, view or change a lasting goal for a long-running task.
commands.details: /goal followed by an objective (up to 4,000 characters) attaches a goal to the chat, and a bare /goal shows it. /goal edit, pause, resume and clear manage it. Needs the goals feature, which is on by default in 0.161.0.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not read goals yet; set them in the session.

commands.name: /agents
commands.summary: Open the agent command center for sessions on the background server.
commands.details: Lists tasks on the shared local background server with their state (working, needs input, ready) and lets you start, resume, rename or archive them. Without a running background server it offers to start one, leaving the current session where it is. The shell version is codex agents.

signalbox.note: Sessions lists recent Codex sessions from ~/.codex/sessions with busy or idle state, next to your other agents.

commands.name: /side
commands.summary: Ask a side question in a temporary fork without touching the main chat.
commands.details: Opens a throwaway fork of the current chat with its own transcript, while the footer keeps showing the main chat's status. Text after the command becomes the first side message. Ctrl+C goes back to the main chat. Not available inside another side chat or during a review.

signalbox.note: Happens inside the session.

commands.name: /copy
commands.summary: Copy the latest response, or part of it, to the clipboard.
commands.details: Opens a small picker to copy the whole latest finished response, or a piece of it, as Markdown. Ctrl+O copies the latest response directly. Nothing is available to copy before the first finished response.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stores or shows message content.

commands.name: /export
commands.summary: Save or copy the whole conversation as Markdown.
commands.details: Without arguments it offers to save the transcript to a file or copy it to the clipboard. With a filename it writes the Markdown file directly.
commands.sideEffects: Writes a Markdown file when you give a filename.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stores or shows message content.

commands.name: /raw
commands.summary: Toggle raw scrollback mode for cleaner text selection in the terminal.
commands.details: Raw mode shows transcript text without rich rendering, so selecting and copying in the terminal is easier. Alt+R toggles it too, and tui.raw_output_mode in config.toml sets the default.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /tui
commands.summary: Choose Scrollback or Fullscreen TUI mode for the next launch.
commands.details: Scrollback leaves scrolling, copy and paste to your terminal; Fullscreen scrolls inside Codex's own view. The choice is saved and applies after a restart, and launch flags such as --no-alt-screen still win.
commands.sideEffects: Saves the TUI mode setting.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /diff
commands.summary: Show what changed in Git, untracked files included.
commands.details: Prints staged, unstaged and untracked changes for the session's directory so you can check edits before committing. Outside a Git repository it says so. Works during a task and inside side chats.

signalbox.note: Run git diff yourself, or this in the session.

commands.name: /mention
commands.summary: Insert @ so you can pick a file to attach to the next message.
commands.details: Does the same as typing @: a search popup opens and the chosen path is added to your prompt. Works during a task and inside side chats.

signalbox.note: Composer helper inside the session.

commands.name: /status
commands.summary: Show the session's model, approvals, writable roots, token use and limits.
commands.details: Prints the current configuration, token usage and how much context is left, refreshing rate-limit readings when it can. On a remote connection it also shows the server address and version. Works while a task is running.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows each Codex session's model, context use and token totals; Limits shows the 5-hour and weekly windows Codex recorded. Approval and sandbox settings are not shown.

commands.name: /daemon
commands.summary: Manage the shared local background server that sessions run on.
commands.details: Opens a menu for the background server (the app-server daemon), for example to switch it to this CLI build or install the latest stable release. Updating can restart the server and interrupt work in other sessions. Not available on remote connections.
commands.sideEffects: Can restart the background server and interrupt running or queued work.

signalbox.note: Affects every session on that server; manage it from a terminal.

commands.name: /warnings
commands.summary: Show the warnings and diagnostic details Codex kept from startup and runtime.
commands.details: Lists warnings Codex collected, for example problems loading config or skills, with their details. Works during a task and inside side chats.

signalbox.note: Signalbox Health shows its own checks of ~/.codex, not Codex's internal warnings.

commands.name: /cd
commands.summary: Move the session to another working directory (your home folder by default).
commands.details: Changes where the session works; with no path it goes to ~. It needs an idle main session with nothing queued and does not work for remote workspaces.

signalbox.note: Changes the session; do it there.

commands.name: /pwd
commands.summary: Print the session's current working directory.
commands.details: Shows the directory the session works in. Takes no arguments and works during a task and inside side chats.

signalbox.note: Sessions shows each session's project directory.

commands.name: /usage
commands.summary: View account usage and token activity, or redeem a usage-limit reset.
commands.details: Opens a usage menu with token-activity analytics and any earned limit resets you can redeem. /usage daily, weekly or cumulative jumps straight to that view. Needs a ChatGPT sign-in.
commands.sideEffects: Redeeming a reset uses it up on your account.

signalbox.note: Usage shows tokens and API-price dollars by day, model and project from rollout files; Limits shows the rate-limit windows. Redeeming resets is not offered.

commands.name: /debug-config
commands.summary: Show config layers and where requirements come from, lowest precedence first.
commands.details: Prints every config layer with its on/off state, then the sources of policy requirements such as allowed approval policies, sandbox modes, MCP servers and rules. Use it when an effective setting differs from config.toml.

signalbox.note: Codex-internal diagnostics.

commands.name: /title
commands.summary: Choose what appears in the terminal window or tab title.
commands.details: Choose which items show and in what order: project, status, thread, branch, model, task progress and more. The title changes at once and the choice is saved to tui.terminal_title in config.toml.
commands.sideEffects: Writes your choice to tui.terminal_title in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /statusline
commands.summary: Choose and reorder the items in the footer status line.
commands.details: Items include model and reasoning, context stats, rate limits, git branch, token counters, session id, directory and version. The footer updates at once and the choice is saved to tui.status_line in config.toml.
commands.sideEffects: Writes your choice to tui.status_line in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /theme
commands.summary: Pick a syntax-highlighting theme with a live preview.
commands.details: Previews each theme as you move through the list and saves the one you confirm to tui.theme in config.toml. It changes how code and diffs are coloured in the transcript.
commands.sideEffects: Writes the chosen theme to tui.theme in config.toml.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /pets
commands.summary: Choose a terminal pet, or hide it.
commands.details: Opens a picker of built-in and custom ambient pets, shown in terminals that can draw images. /pets off (also hide or none) turns it off, and a pet id picks one directly. The choice is saved.
commands.sideEffects: Saves the pet choice.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI setting.

commands.name: /mcp
commands.summary: List MCP servers and their tools; /mcp verbose adds server details.
commands.details: Shows the MCP tools this session can call and each server's sign-in state. /mcp verbose adds full server diagnostics, and /mcp login <name> starts an OAuth sign-in for that server.
commands.sideEffects: /mcp login stores OAuth tokens for that server.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not track MCP health for Codex; codex mcp list shows configured servers.

commands.name: /apps
commands.summary: List the apps (connectors) Codex can use; mention one as $app-slug.
commands.details: Prints the apps available to this session. In 0.161.0 it is left out of the slash popup but still works when typed, as long as apps are enabled. Mention an app in a prompt with $ and its slug.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /plugins
commands.summary: Browse installed and available plugins, and switch them on or off.
commands.details: Opens a plugin browser with marketplace tabs where you can see a plugin's skills and tools, install suggested ones and enable or disable installed ones with Space. Shown when plugins are enabled, which is the default.
commands.sideEffects: Installing or toggling a plugin changes your Codex config and plugin cache.

signalbox.note: Signalbox lists the skills of installed plugins but does not manage plugins.

commands.name: /logout
commands.summary: Sign out of Codex and remove the stored credentials.
commands.details: Clears the saved login for this Codex home. You need to sign in again before the next session.
commands.sideEffects: Deletes stored Codex credentials.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never touches credentials.

commands.name: /quit
commands.summary: Exit Codex.
commands.details: Closes the TUI at once, without a confirmation. The session stays saved and can be resumed later. Ctrl+C also exits.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stops sessions it did not start.

commands.name: /feedback
commands.summary: Send feedback, and logs if you choose, to the Codex maintainers.
commands.details: Asks for a category and whether to include logs and diagnostics, then uploads them to OpenAI. If your config turns feedback off, it says so instead.
commands.sideEffects: Uploads logs and diagnostics to OpenAI when you include them.

signalbox.note: Sends data off the machine; only you should do that, in the session.

commands.name: /rollout
commands.summary: Print the path of this session's rollout file (debug builds only).
commands.details: It is compiled into the binary but hidden in release builds. The npm build of 0.161.0 therefore neither lists nor runs it.

signalbox.note: Signalbox finds rollout files under ~/.codex/sessions on its own.

commands.name: /ps
commands.summary: See background terminals and the last few lines each printed.
commands.details: Shows each background terminal's command with up to three recent output lines, so you can check long-running commands without leaving the chat. The list can be empty when unified exec is not in use.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not see a session's background terminals.

commands.name: /stop
commands.summary: Stop every background terminal this session started.
commands.details: Ends the session's background terminal processes. Works while a task is running.
commands.sideEffects: Kills the session's background processes.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stops processes it did not start.

commands.name: /clear
commands.summary: Wipe the terminal and begin a new chat.
commands.details: Wipes the terminal view and starts a new chat in the same Codex window; the previous chat stays saved. A name after the command titles the new chat. Ctrl+L only clears the screen and keeps the current chat.

signalbox.note: Happens inside the session.

commands.name: /test-approval
commands.summary: Show a fake file-change approval prompt (debug builds only).
commands.details: A developer test that is compiled in but hidden in release builds. The npm build of 0.161.0 therefore neither lists nor runs it.

signalbox.note: Developer test only.

commands.name: /subagents
commands.summary: Switch between the subagent threads of this session.
commands.details: Opens a picker of agent threads spawned in this session so you can watch or continue one. The docs also call it /agent, but 0.161.0 only accepts /subagents.

signalbox.note: Switching threads happens in the TUI.

commands.name: /debug-m-drop
commands.summary: Internal memory-maintenance command, marked do not use.
commands.details: Left out of the slash popup. In 0.161.0 it only prints a notice that memory maintenance is not available from this TUI.

signalbox.note: Internal maintenance command.

commands.name: /debug-m-update
commands.summary: Internal memory-maintenance command, marked do not use.
commands.details: Left out of the slash popup. In 0.161.0 it only prints a notice that memory maintenance is not available from this TUI.

signalbox.note: Internal maintenance command.

commands.name: /reasoning
commands.summary: Desktop app only: pick how hard the model reasons in this chat.
commands.details: Part of the ChatGPT desktop app's composer, not the CLI. In the terminal, /model covers reasoning effort.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /ide-context
commands.summary: Turn shared IDE context on or off (desktop app only).
commands.details: The desktop app's counterpart to /ide in the terminal. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /pin
commands.summary: Pin or unpin the current chat (desktop app only).
commands.details: Keeps a chat at the top of the desktop app's chat list, when the app offers pinning. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /project
commands.summary: Choose the project that new chats use (desktop app only).
commands.details: Sets which local project the desktop app starts new chats in. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /chat
commands.summary: Pick a chat with no project before starting a new one (desktop app only).
commands.details: Lets the desktop app start a chat that is not tied to a local project. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /local
commands.summary: Run the chat in the selected local project (desktop app only).
commands.details: Switches a desktop app chat to run on this machine rather than in the cloud. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

commands.name: /cloud
commands.summary: Run the chat in Codex Cloud, when cloud runs are available (desktop app only).
commands.details: Sends the desktop app chat to a cloud environment instead of this machine. Cloud sessions do not leave rollout files here, so Signalbox cannot see them.

signalbox.note: Cloud runs leave nothing on this machine for Signalbox to read.

commands.name: /cloud-environment
commands.summary: Choose the cloud environment for the chat (desktop app only).
commands.details: Picks which configured Codex Cloud environment a desktop app chat runs in. It is not available in the Codex CLI.

signalbox.note: Run it in the desktop app.

cliCommands.name: codex resume
cliCommands.summary: Reopen a saved interactive session, from a picker or by id or name.
cliCommands.details: --last continues the most recent session for this directory without the picker, and --all shows sessions from every directory. --include-non-interactive also lists codex exec runs. It accepts the usual launch flags such as -m and -s.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never resumes sessions. Select the session in History and use Copy under Resume, then paste the line into a terminal.

cliCommands.name: codex fork
cliCommands.summary: Start a new interactive session from a copy of a saved one.
cliCommands.details: Opens a picker by default; --last forks the most recent session. The original session is left unchanged.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself in a terminal.

cliCommands.name: codex exec
cliCommands.summary: Run one task without the TUI and print the result.
cliCommands.details: The prompt can come from stdin with -. --json streams events as JSON lines, -o writes the final message to a file and --output-schema constrains the final answer. --ephemeral skips saving the session to disk. Slash commands are not interpreted here; use the subcommands instead.

signalbox.note: Saved exec runs show up in Signalbox like other sessions; --ephemeral runs leave no rollout to read.

cliCommands.name: codex exec resume
cliCommands.summary: Send a follow-up prompt to a saved session without the TUI.
cliCommands.details: Picks the session by id, name or --last, sends the prompt and prints the outcome. Takes the same output flags as codex exec.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Adds a turn to an existing session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never messages sessions it did not create.

cliCommands.name: codex review
cliCommands.summary: Run a code review without the TUI.
cliCommands.details: Choose one target: uncommitted changes, the diff against a base branch, a single commit, or custom instructions as the prompt. --title labels a commit review. codex exec review does the same with exec's output flags.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself; it costs model usage.

cliCommands.name: codex agents
cliCommands.summary: See every session hosted by the shared background server on this machine.
cliCommands.details: Opens the agent command center as its own TUI, listing sessions on the app-server daemon with their state. Use --remote to look at a remote server.

signalbox.note: Sessions lists Codex sessions from rollout files, together with your other agents.

cliCommands.name: codex queue
cliCommands.summary: Line up a message for another session to pick up when it's ready.
cliCommands.details: Picks the session by UUID or exact name. The message waits in that session's queue until it can take input.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Sends input into another session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never messages sessions it did not create.

cliCommands.name: codex archive
cliCommands.summary: Hide a saved session from lists, by id or name; nothing is deleted.
cliCommands.details: Hides the session from pickers without deleting its transcript. A UUID wins over a name that looks the same.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Moves the session out of active lists.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not change sessions.

cliCommands.name: codex unarchive
cliCommands.summary: Bring an archived session back by id or name.
cliCommands.details: Restores a session that /archive or codex archive hid. A UUID wins over a name that looks the same.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not change sessions.

cliCommands.name: codex delete
cliCommands.summary: Delete a saved session for good, chosen by id or name.
cliCommands.details: Asks for confirmation unless --force is given. --force only works with a UUID, so a name always gets a prompt.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Deletes the transcript for good.

signalbox.note: Destructive.

cliCommands.name: codex login status
cliCommands.summary: Show whether Codex is signed in and how.
cliCommands.details: Reports the current login method without changing it. To answer, Codex reads its stored credentials.

signalbox.note: It reads stored credentials; Signalbox stays away from auth.

cliCommands.name: codex login
cliCommands.summary: Sign in with ChatGPT, a device code, an API key or an access token.
cliCommands.details: Without options it signs in with ChatGPT in the browser, and --device-auth uses a device code instead. The API key and access token options read the secret from stdin.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Stores credentials in the Codex home.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never touches credentials.

cliCommands.name: codex logout
cliCommands.summary: Remove the stored Codex credentials.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Deletes stored credentials.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never touches credentials.

cliCommands.name: codex mcp list
cliCommands.summary: List the MCP servers configured for Codex.
cliCommands.details: Reads the servers from your Codex config without starting them. The related codex mcp get <NAME> shows one server, and both accept --json.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself; Signalbox does not track MCP servers for Codex.

cliCommands.name: codex mcp add
cliCommands.summary: Add an MCP server, either a local command or a streamable HTTP URL.
cliCommands.details: Local servers can get environment variables with --env; HTTP servers can read a bearer token from an environment variable or use OAuth options. codex mcp remove <NAME> deletes an entry.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.codex/config.toml.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: codex mcp login
cliCommands.summary: Sign in to an MCP server with OAuth (codex mcp logout signs out).
cliCommands.details: Opens a browser unless --no-browser is given. --scopes asks for specific OAuth scopes.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Stores or removes OAuth tokens.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never touches credentials.

cliCommands.name: codex plugin list
cliCommands.summary: Show plugins offered by your configured marketplaces and remote ones.
cliCommands.details: Use -m to limit it to one marketplace. With --json, --available also includes plugins that are not installed.

signalbox.note: Signalbox lists installed plugin skills from the plugin cache instead of running this.

cliCommands.name: codex plugin add
cliCommands.summary: Install a plugin (codex plugin remove uninstalls one).
cliCommands.details: Installs from a configured or remote marketplace into the plugin cache. codex plugin marketplace add, list, upgrade and remove manage the marketplace sources.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Changes the plugin cache and Codex config.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not manage plugins.

cliCommands.name: codex features list
cliCommands.summary: List feature flags with their stage and whether they are on.
cliCommands.details: The related codex features enable <NAME> and disable <NAME> change a flag permanently in config.toml. The --enable and --disable flags on any command change it for one run.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex doctor
cliCommands.summary: Check the Codex install, config, auth and runtime health.
cliCommands.details: With --json it prints a redacted machine-readable report. With --summary it shows only the grouped results and the final count.

signalbox.note: Signalbox Health covers what it can read from ~/.codex; run this for Codex's own checks.

cliCommands.name: codex update
cliCommands.summary: Upgrade Codex to the newest release.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Replaces the installed Codex binary.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex app
cliCommands.summary: Open the ChatGPT desktop app on a workspace, installing it if missing.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex apply
cliCommands.summary: Apply the latest diff from a Codex Cloud task to your working tree.
cliCommands.details: It runs the patch through git apply. Conflicts make it exit with an error.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Changes files in your working tree.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex cloud
cliCommands.summary: Browse, start and apply Codex Cloud tasks from the terminal (experimental).
cliCommands.details: Without a subcommand it opens a picker. list and status inspect tasks, diff shows a task's patch, apply brings it into the working tree and exec submits a new task.

signalbox.note: Cloud tasks leave no rollout files on this machine.

cliCommands.name: codex debug models
cliCommands.summary: Dump the model catalog Codex uses, as raw JSON.
cliCommands.details: By default it may refresh the catalog from OpenAI first. With --bundled it prints only the catalog shipped with this binary.

signalbox.note: Signalbox keeps its own model table.

cliCommands.name: codex debug prompt-input
cliCommands.summary: Print the prompt input the model would see, as JSON.
cliCommands.details: Useful for checking which instruction files and context Codex picks up. The output contains your instruction text.

signalbox.note: Contains prompt content, which Signalbox never shows.

cliCommands.name: codex sandbox
cliCommands.summary: Run a command inside Codex's sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS).
cliCommands.details: Handy for checking what a sandboxed command can reach. --log-denials prints macOS sandbox denials after the command exits.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex completion
cliCommands.summary: Print a shell completion script.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex app-server daemon
cliCommands.summary: Manage the local background server that interactive sessions share.
cliCommands.details: The version subcommand prints the CLI and running server versions as JSON. The stop, restart and update subcommands can interrupt work in every session on that server.
cliCommands.sideEffects: stop, restart and update can interrupt running sessions.

signalbox.note: Affects every session on the server; run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: codex remote-control
cliCommands.summary: Run the background server with remote control on, or pair a device (experimental).
cliCommands.details: The start subcommand launches the background server with remote control on, and stop stops it. The pair subcommand prints a short-lived pairing code.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Lets a paired device control sessions on this machine.

signalbox.note: Opening remote access is the user's decision.

cliCommands.name: codex migrate-rollouts
cliCommands.summary: Check, or with --apply perform, the move of old sessions to paged history.
cliCommands.details: Without --apply it only reports which sessions qualify. Migrating changes how Codex stores session history on disk.
cliCommands.sideEffects: --apply rewrites how saved sessions are stored.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself. Signalbox reads rollout files, so check its Health view after migrating.

cliCommands.name: codex --no-alt-screen
cliCommands.summary: Run the TUI inline so your terminal keeps its scrollback.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex -m
cliCommands.summary: Start a session on a specific model without changing your default.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex -s
cliCommands.summary: Choose the sandbox for commands the model runs in this session.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex -a
cliCommands.summary: Choose when Codex must ask before running a command.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex -p
cliCommands.summary: Layer $CODEX_HOME/<NAME>.config.toml over your base config for this run.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex -c
cliCommands.summary: Override one config.toml value for this run only.
cliCommands.details: Use a dotted path for nested keys. The value is read as TOML, or as a plain string if that fails.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex --search
cliCommands.summary: Turn on live web search for the session.
cliCommands.details: Without it, web search uses cached results. With it, the model can search the live web without asking each time.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex --worktree
cliCommands.summary: Run the session in a new Git worktree that Codex manages.

signalbox.note: Launch flag.

cliCommands.name: codex --no-daemon
cliCommands.summary: Start a session in its own process, not on the shared background server.
cliCommands.details: The session runs in its own process instead of on the background server. Tools that list the server's sessions, such as codex agents, may not show it.

signalbox.note: Launch flag. Signalbox still sees the session through its rollout file.

cliCommands.name: codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
cliCommands.summary: Run commands with no sandbox and no approval prompts.
cliCommands.details: Meant only for machines that are already isolated, such as a throwaway VM or container. For ordinary work, --add-dir or the workspace-write sandbox is the safer way to grant access.
cliCommands.sideEffects: The agent can change anything your user account can.

signalbox.note: Never suggested by Signalbox.

commands.name: /about
commands.summary: Shows the CLI version, OS, sandbox, current model, sign-in method and tier.
commands.details: Prints an info card in the session, meant for pasting into bug reports. Editors that run gemini --acp get it too.

signalbox.note: The command guide shows the installed Gemini CLI version. Model, auth and tier need the session, and there is no Gemini adapter yet.

commands.name: /agents
commands.summary: Lists and manages subagents: built-in, local and remote.
commands.details: With no argument it lists every agent it found. reload (alias refresh) rescans ~/.gemini/agents and .gemini/agents. enable and disable save an override; config opens a dialog for an agent's model, temperature and limits. It is hidden when experimental.enableAgents is off (it is on by default).
commands.sideEffects: enable, disable and config write agents.overrides to settings.json.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session. Signalbox does not track Gemini subagents.

commands.name: /auth
commands.summary: Signs in, changes the auth method, or signs out.
commands.details: Bare /auth (or signin, alias login) opens the sign-in dialog. signout (alias logout) deletes the cached credentials, clears the saved auth type and then offers to sign in again or exit.
commands.sideEffects: signout removes cached credentials and edits security.auth.selectedType in user settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never touches sign-in or credentials. Run it yourself in the session.

commands.name: /bug
commands.summary: Opens a prefilled GitHub issue with version and environment details.
commands.details: The text after /bug becomes the issue title. If the session has any conversation it also exports the chat history to a JSON file in the project temp folder so you can attach it. advanced.bugCommand can point it at another URL.
commands.sideEffects: Opens the browser. May write bug-report-history-<time>.json under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session if you want to file a Gemini CLI bug.

commands.name: /bug-memory
commands.summary: Saves a V8 heap snapshot of the running CLI for a bug report.
commands.details: It can take 20 seconds or more and the UI freezes meanwhile. The .heapsnapshot file goes to the project temp folder. Not in the docs.
commands.sideEffects: Writes a large bug-memory-<time>.heapsnapshot under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/. It can contain secrets and conversation text from memory.

signalbox.note: Heap snapshots can hold credentials and message content, so Signalbox never offers it.

commands.name: /clear
commands.summary: Clears the screen and starts a fresh session with a new session ID.
commands.details: Runs the SessionEnd and SessionStart hooks and resets the conversation and the session stats. The old session stays on disk and /resume can reopen it. Ctrl+L only redraws the screen and keeps the conversation.
commands.sideEffects: Drops the conversation context and changes the session ID.

signalbox.note: Not offered because it discards context. Run it in the session.

commands.name: /commands
commands.summary: Lists or reloads your custom slash commands (.toml files).
commands.details: list shows the .toml files in ~/.gemini/commands, the project's .gemini/commands and active extensions. reload (alias refresh) picks up new or edited files, MCP prompts and extension commands without a restart.

signalbox.note: The Signalbox command guide lists the same custom commands with their descriptions (names and descriptions only, never the prompt text).

commands.name: /compress
commands.summary: Replaces the conversation so far with a summary to free up context.
commands.details: The model writes the summary, so it costs tokens. Gemini also compresses by itself once context use passes model.compressionThreshold (half the window by default).
commands.sideEffects: The summary replaces the earlier turns for the rest of the session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox has no way to run commands inside a Gemini session. Copy it and run it there.

commands.name: /copy
commands.summary: Copies the model's last reply to the clipboard.
commands.details: Uses pbcopy on macOS. Over SSH it falls back to the OSC 52 terminal escape, which the terminal must support.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stores or shows message content.

commands.name: /corgi
commands.summary: Hidden easter egg that toggles corgi mode in the UI.
commands.details: Not shown in /help or in the docs.

signalbox.note: Cosmetic only.

commands.name: /directory
commands.summary: Adds folders to this session's workspace, or lists them.
commands.details: add takes absolute, relative or ~ paths separated by commas; a folder you have not trusted asks for trust first. show lists folders added this way or with --include-directories. Restrictive sandbox profiles block add, so use --include-directories at launch instead.
commands.sideEffects: Lasts for this session only. The model can then read and edit files in those folders.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /docs
commands.summary: Takes you to the Gemini CLI docs website.
commands.details: Inside a container sandbox it prints the URL instead of opening it.
commands.sideEffects: Opens a browser tab.

signalbox.note: Open https://geminicli.com/docs directly.

commands.name: /editor
commands.summary: Chooses the external editor used for editing input and diffs.
commands.sideEffects: Saves general.preferredEditor in settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

commands.name: /export-session
commands.summary: Writes the full record of the current session to a JSON file.
commands.details: The path is relative to the current folder. The file holds the whole conversation, tool calls and stats. Not in the docs; /resume share writes a readable transcript instead.
commands.sideEffects: Writes a file that contains conversation content.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never stores or shows message content.

commands.name: /extensions
commands.args: [list | update <names>|--all | explore | reload | install | uninstall | link | enable | disable | config]
commands.summary: Lists, updates and manages Gemini CLI extensions.
commands.details: With no argument it lists active extensions. explore opens the extension gallery, update updates named extensions or all of them, reload (alias restart) reloads them. install, uninstall (alias delete), link, enable, disable and config only appear when experimental.extensionReloading is on; otherwise use the gemini extensions shell command. Editors using --acp get it too.
commands.sideEffects: install, update, uninstall and link change ~/.gemini/extensions; enable and disable change extension-enablement.json.

signalbox.note: The command guide lists the commands and skills that extensions add, but Signalbox does not manage extensions.

commands.name: /footer
commands.summary: Chooses which items the footer status line shows.
commands.details: Items include the folder, git branch, sandbox, model, context use, quota use, memory, session ID, line changes and token totals. Not in the commands docs.
commands.sideEffects: Saves ui.footer settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

commands.name: /help
commands.summary: Shows the built-in help: commands and keyboard shortcuts.
commands.details: Typing ? on an empty prompt toggles the shortcuts panel instead. The docs still mention a /? alias, but this version does not register it.

signalbox.note: The Signalbox command guide covers the same built-in commands, plus your custom ones.

commands.name: /hooks
commands.summary: Lists registered hooks and turns them on or off.
commands.details: Bare /hooks (or panel, list, show) lists the hooks with their status. enable and disable act on one hook; enable-all and disable-all on every hook. It is hidden when hooksConfig.enabled is false (it is on by default).
commands.sideEffects: enable and disable rewrite hooksConfig.disabled in workspace or user settings.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /ide
commands.summary: Connects Gemini CLI to your editor: VS Code and editors built on it, JetBrains and more.
commands.details: Once connected it can see your open files; supported editors include VS Code and editors built on it such as Cursor, JetBrains IDEs, Antigravity, Sublime Text and several cloud IDEs. status shows whether it is connected and which files are open. install adds the companion extension to the IDE; enable and disable switch the integration. Outside a supported IDE's terminal it only prints an error.
commands.sideEffects: enable and disable save ide.enabled in user settings; install adds an extension to the IDE.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /init
commands.summary: Creates a GEMINI.md for the project and has the model fill it in.
commands.details: Writes an empty GEMINI.md in the project root, then sends a prompt to analyse the project, so it costs a model turn. Does nothing if GEMINI.md already exists. Editors using --acp get it too.
commands.sideEffects: Creates GEMINI.md in the project root, which the model then writes.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /mcp
commands.args: [list | desc | schema | auth <server> | reload | enable <server> | disable <server>] [--session]
commands.summary: Shows configured MCP servers with their tools, and manages them.
commands.details: Bare /mcp (or list, ls) lists servers, tools, prompts and resources; desc adds descriptions and schema adds input schemas. reload (alias refresh) restarts the servers. enable and disable are saved unless you add --session; auth runs an OAuth sign-in for one server.
commands.sideEffects: enable and disable write ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json and restart the servers; auth stores OAuth tokens.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start or manage MCP servers and never handles their tokens.

commands.name: /memory
commands.summary: Shows, lists or reloads the GEMINI.md instructions given to the model.
commands.details: show prints the combined GEMINI.md text, list prints the file paths and reload (alias refresh) reads them again. inbox reviews skills and memory changes that Auto Memory pulled from past sessions (needs experimental.autoMemory). There is no /memory add in this version. Editors using --acp get it too.
commands.sideEffects: inbox can apply patches and move skills into your skills folders.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never reads GEMINI.md content.

commands.name: /model
commands.summary: Opens the model picker, or switches the model directly.
commands.details: Bare /model (or manage) opens a dialog that also shows quota, with a switch to remember the choice. set changes the model for this session only, unless you add --persist.
commands.sideEffects: set --persist, or the dialog's remember option, saves model.name in user settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox has no way to run commands inside a Gemini session. Per-model usage needs a Gemini adapter, which is not built yet.

commands.name: /permissions
commands.summary: Opens the folder-trust dialog for the current folder or another one.
commands.details: Trust decides whether a folder's project settings, commands, skills, hooks and MCP servers load. It only exists while folder trust is on (the default).
commands.sideEffects: Saves the choice in ~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json.

signalbox.note: Trust is a security decision. Signalbox never makes or offers it.

commands.name: /plan
commands.summary: Switches to read-only Plan Mode and shows the approved plan, if any.
commands.details: Text after /plan is sent as a prompt in Plan Mode. copy puts the approved plan on the clipboard. Shift+Tab also cycles the approval modes. It exists while general.plan.enabled is on (the default).
commands.sideEffects: Changes the approval mode for this session.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /policies
commands.summary: Lists the active policy-engine rules, grouped by approval mode.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /privacy
commands.summary: Shows the privacy notice and lets you change data-collection consent.
commands.details: The notice depends on the sign-in type. On a free Google tier you can opt in or out of your data being used to improve Google's products.
commands.sideEffects: A free-tier consent change is saved to your Google account.

signalbox.note: Consent is yours to give. Signalbox never offers it.

commands.name: /quit
commands.summary: Exits Gemini CLI and prints a short session summary.
commands.details: With --delete it also permanently removes this session's recording and temporary files on the way out.
commands.sideEffects: --delete permanently deletes the session history.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never ends a session it did not start.

commands.name: /restore
commands.summary: Rolls files and the conversation back to just before a tool call.
commands.details: Without an ID it lists the checkpoints. It only exists when general.checkpointing.enabled is on (off by default); snapshots live in a shadow git repo under ~/.gemini/history/<project>. Editors using --acp get it too.
commands.sideEffects: Overwrites project files with the checkpoint and rewinds the conversation.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /resume
commands.summary: Browses auto-saved sessions to resume, and manages tagged checkpoints.
commands.details: Bare /resume opens a session browser with search, sorting and delete. save, resume (alias load), delete and list handle named checkpoints for this project; share writes the conversation to a .md or .json file. /chat is the same command.
commands.sideEffects: save writes and delete removes checkpoint files under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/; share writes a transcript; deleting in the browser removes a session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never resumes Gemini sessions. A future Gemini adapter could list past sessions, without their content.

commands.name: /rewind
commands.summary: Goes back to an earlier prompt and can undo the file changes made since.
commands.details: Pick a past message, then rewind the conversation, revert the file edits, or both. Pressing Esc twice on an empty prompt opens it too.
commands.sideEffects: Can revert file edits made after that message and drop the later turns.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /settings
commands.summary: Opens the settings editor for user and workspace settings.
commands.details: A searchable list of every setting with validation. Some changes apply at once, others after a restart.
commands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.gemini/settings.json or the project's .gemini/settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

commands.name: /setup-github
commands.summary: Adds GitHub Actions workflows that run Gemini on issues and pull requests.
commands.details: Must run inside a git repository with a GitHub remote. Downloads workflow and command files from the latest run-gemini-cli release into .github/workflows and .github/commands, updates .gitignore and opens the setup guide.
commands.sideEffects: Downloads files into the repository and edits .gitignore.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /shortcuts
commands.summary: Shows or hides the shortcut cheat sheet above the prompt.
commands.details: Same as typing ? on an empty prompt. Not in the commands docs.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI only.

commands.name: /skills
commands.summary: Lists, links, enables, disables or reloads agent skills.
commands.details: Bare /skills lists them. link adds skills from a local folder for you or for the workspace. enable and disable are saved in settings; reload (alias refresh) rescans the skill folders. Every enabled skill can also be called as /<skill-name>.
commands.sideEffects: link creates links in a skills folder; enable and disable update skills.disabled in settings.

signalbox.note: The command guide lists your skills as /<name> commands (name and description only). Managing them needs the session.

commands.name: /stats
commands.summary: Shows this session's usage: duration, tokens per model, tool calls and quota.
commands.details: session (the default) shows duration, tool calls and, when signed in with Google, remaining quota and reset time. model breaks tokens down per model, with cached tokens where reported. tools shows call counts and timing per tool.

signalbox.note: Not yet: a Gemini adapter would read token counts from chat recordings in ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats. Gemini quota is not available to Signalbox.

commands.name: /tasks
commands.summary: Toggles the panel of background tasks, such as shells sent to the background.
commands.details: The docs still call this /shells (or /bashes). This version registers /tasks with the aliases /bg and /background instead.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI only.

commands.name: /terminal-setup
commands.summary: Adds newline and undo keybindings to VS Code, Cursor or Windsurf.
commands.details: Finds the editor whose terminal you are in and adds Shift+Enter and Ctrl+Enter for new lines, plus undo and redo keys, to its keybindings.json. Restart the terminal afterwards.
commands.sideEffects: Edits the editor's keybindings.json.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /theme
commands.summary: Opens the colour theme picker.
commands.sideEffects: Saves ui.theme in settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

commands.name: /tools
commands.summary: Lists the tools the model can call right now.
commands.details: desc (alias descriptions) adds each tool's full description as the model sees it.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /upgrade
commands.summary: Opens the Gemini Code Assist upgrade page for higher limits.
commands.details: Only exists when you sign in with Google. On an Ultra tier it just says you are already on the top tier.
commands.sideEffects: Opens a browser tab.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /vim
commands.summary: Turns vim-style editing of the prompt on or off.
commands.details: Adds NORMAL and INSERT modes with counts, motions, edits such as dd and cw, and . to repeat.
commands.sideEffects: Saves general.vimMode in user settings.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

commands.name: /gemma
commands.summary: Checks the local Gemma model routing setup and its server.
commands.details: Shows whether the LiteRT-LM binary and the model are installed, whether the local server is running and whether routing is on. Set it up or start it with the gemini gemma shell command. Not in the commands docs.

signalbox.note: Run it in the session.

commands.name: /voice
commands.summary: Toggles voice dictation; model picks the transcription model.
commands.details: Experimental and off by default. It only appears when experimental.voiceMode is true.

signalbox.note: Terminal UI only.

commands.name: @<path>
commands.summary: Puts a file's or folder's contents into your prompt.
commands.details: Folders are read recursively and git-ignored files are skipped by default. Escape spaces with a backslash. It uses the read_many_files tool and also works with -p.

signalbox.note: Prompt syntax, not a command Signalbox can run.

commands.name: !<command>
commands.summary: Runs a shell command from the prompt; a lone ! toggles shell mode.
commands.details: On macOS and Linux it runs through bash with your own permissions and sets GEMINI_CLI=1 for the child process. In shell mode every line goes to the shell until you toggle it off.
commands.sideEffects: Runs any command with your permissions.

signalbox.note: Prompt syntax, not a command Signalbox can run.

cliCommands.name: gemini --version
cliCommands.summary: Prints the installed Gemini CLI version.

signalbox.note: Signalbox runs this to show the installed version in signalbox doctor and in the command guide.

cliCommands.name: gemini --help
cliCommands.summary: Lists the shell subcommands and launch flags.
cliCommands.details: Each subcommand has its own help too, for example gemini mcp --help.

signalbox.note: The command guide summarises the most useful flags.

cliCommands.name: gemini
cliCommands.summary: Starts an interactive session, optionally with a first prompt.
cliCommands.details: Without a terminal attached (for example from a script) it switches to headless mode instead.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini -p
cliCommands.summary: Runs one prompt without the interactive UI and prints the answer.
cliCommands.details: Text piped on stdin is added to the prompt. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 42 bad input, 53 turn limit. Custom slash commands and @ paths work here; most built-in slash commands do not.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Calls the model (uses quota) and records a new session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --output-format
cliCommands.summary: Picks headless output: plain text, one JSON object, or a JSONL event stream.
cliCommands.details: json returns the reply plus token and latency stats. stream-json emits init, message, tool_use, tool_result, error and result events; result carries per-model token totals.

signalbox.note: Only useful for runs you start yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini -i
cliCommands.summary: Runs a first prompt and then stays in the interactive session.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --resume
cliCommands.summary: Reopens a saved session for the current folder.
cliCommands.details: latest picks the most recent one; an index comes from --list-sessions. Add a prompt to continue straight away, or -p to continue headless.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never resumes a session it did not create.

cliCommands.name: gemini --list-sessions
cliCommands.summary: Lists saved sessions for the current folder and exits.
cliCommands.details: Each line shows an index, the session title (often its first prompt), the age and the session ID. History is per project, so run it from the project folder.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Prints session titles, which can contain prompt text. May register the folder in ~/.gemini/projects.json.

signalbox.note: It prints message text, so Signalbox does not run it. A future Gemini adapter would read session files directly.

cliCommands.name: gemini --delete-session
cliCommands.summary: Deletes a saved session and its related files.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Permanently removes the session recording, plans, tool outputs and logs.

signalbox.note: Destructive. Signalbox never deletes agent data.

cliCommands.name: gemini --session-id
cliCommands.summary: Starts a new session with an ID you choose.
cliCommands.details: Useful when a script wants to find the session's files later.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --model
cliCommands.summary: Starts with a given model or alias for this run only.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --approval-mode
cliCommands.summary: Sets how tool calls are approved for this run.
cliCommands.details: default asks each time, auto_edit approves file edits, yolo approves everything (same as -y/--yolo) and plan is read-only.
cliCommands.sideEffects: yolo runs every tool call without asking.

signalbox.note: Your choice at launch. Signalbox never changes approval settings.

cliCommands.name: gemini --worktree
cliCommands.summary: Starts the session in a new git worktree.
cliCommands.details: A name is generated when you leave it out.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Creates a git worktree and branch.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --include-directories
cliCommands.summary: Adds more folders to the workspace at launch.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --sandbox
cliCommands.summary: Runs tools inside a sandbox (macOS Seatbelt or a container).

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini --skip-trust
cliCommands.summary: Trusts the current folder for this session only.

signalbox.note: Trust is a security decision. Signalbox never makes or offers it.

cliCommands.name: gemini --acp
cliCommands.summary: Runs as an Agent Client Protocol server for editors such as Zed.
cliCommands.details: Editors talk to it over stdio. Only a few slash commands exist there: /about, /help, /init, /memory, /extensions and /restore.

signalbox.note: For editor integrations, not something Signalbox runs.

cliCommands.name: gemini --list-extensions
cliCommands.summary: Lists the installed extensions and exits.

signalbox.note: The command guide shows the commands and skills extensions add.

cliCommands.name: gemini --extensions
cliCommands.summary: Loads only the named extensions for this run.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start agent sessions.

cliCommands.name: gemini mcp list
cliCommands.summary: Lists configured MCP servers with their connection status.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Connects to every server to check it, which starts local stdio servers.

signalbox.note: Signalbox does not start MCP servers, so it does not run this.

cliCommands.name: gemini mcp add
cliCommands.summary: Adds an MCP server (stdio command or HTTP URL) to settings.
cliCommands.details: Options cover transport, environment variables, scope (user or project) and tool filters.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes mcpServers in user or project settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini mcp remove
cliCommands.summary: Removes an MCP server from settings.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Edits settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini mcp enable
cliCommands.summary: Turns a disabled MCP server back on.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini mcp disable
cliCommands.summary: Disables an MCP server without removing its config.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions list
cliCommands.summary: Lists installed extensions.

signalbox.note: The command guide shows the commands and skills extensions add.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions install
cliCommands.summary: Adds an extension, taken from a git URL or a folder on disk.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Downloads code into ~/.gemini/extensions; the extension can add commands, hooks and MCP servers.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself after reviewing the source.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions uninstall
cliCommands.summary: Uninstalls one or more extensions.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Deletes the extension folders.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions update
cliCommands.summary: Updates one extension, or all of them, to the latest version.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Downloads new extension code.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions enable
cliCommands.summary: Enables an extension for the user or a workspace.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.gemini/extensions/extension-enablement.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions disable
cliCommands.summary: Disables an extension for the user or a workspace.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes ~/.gemini/extensions/extension-enablement.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions link
cliCommands.summary: Links a local extension folder so edits there apply right away.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Adds an entry under ~/.gemini/extensions that points at the folder.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions new
cliCommands.summary: Creates a new extension from a starter template.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Creates files at the given path.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions validate
cliCommands.summary: Checks a local extension folder for problems.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini extensions config
cliCommands.summary: Sets an extension's settings, such as API keys it needs.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Stores values in the extension's .env file or the system keychain.

signalbox.note: May handle secrets. Signalbox never touches them.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills list
cliCommands.summary: Lists discovered agent skills; --all includes built-in ones.

signalbox.note: The command guide lists enabled skills as /<name> commands.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills install
cliCommands.summary: Installs a skill from a git URL or a local path.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Copies files into ~/.gemini/skills or the project's .gemini/skills.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills link
cliCommands.summary: Links skills from a local folder so edits there apply right away.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Creates symlinks in a skills folder.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills uninstall
cliCommands.summary: Removes an installed skill.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Deletes the skill folder.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills enable
cliCommands.summary: Re-enables a disabled skill.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Edits skills.disabled in settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini skills disable
cliCommands.summary: Disables a skill without deleting it.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Edits skills.disabled in settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini hooks migrate
cliCommands.summary: Copies hooks from the project's Claude Code settings into Gemini CLI.
cliCommands.details: Reads .claude/settings.local.json, or .claude/settings.json, in the current folder, converts the hooks and merges them into the project's Gemini settings.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Writes hooks into the project's .gemini/settings.json.

signalbox.note: Signalbox never writes agent config.

cliCommands.name: gemini gemma setup
cliCommands.summary: Downloads and configures a local Gemma model for routing.
cliCommands.details: Fetches the LiteRT-LM runtime and, unless told to skip it, the model.
cliCommands.sideEffects: Large download; writes experimental.gemmaModelRouter to user and workspace settings.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.

cliCommands.name: gemini gemma status
cliCommands.summary: Checks the local Gemma setup and whether its server is running.
cliCommands.details: gemini gemma start, stop and logs control the local LiteRT-LM server.

signalbox.note: Run it yourself.
